821	---
822	
823	## Multi-mechanism tools + rationale
824	
825	Tools where the install path differs by OS / arch / role-feature-flag,
826	with rationale.
827	
828	| Tool | Mechanism dispatch | Why |
829	|---|---|---|
830	| **uv** | Bootstrap: curl. Later: dispatch between `brew upgrade uv` vs `uv self update` based on binary path | brew installs pin to versioned Cellar — `uv self update` no-ops there. Mirror logic in role + upgrade script keeps both paths working. See [pitfall](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md) |
831	| **OpenCode** | curl-installer on both OSes (2026-05) | Was brew tap (`anomalyco/tap`) on macOS, but formula version lagged + Cellar-pinning broke `opencode upgrade`. Unified on official installer with `--no-modify-path`. See `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml` `# === OpenCode` block |
832	| **OpenAI Codex CLI** | macOS: brew cask; Linux: npm `@openai/codex` | macOS has the brewed `.app` (richer); Linux only ships npm CLI |
833	| **Gemini CLI** | macOS: brew formula `gemini-cli` → npm fallback; Linux: npm | brew formula availability is inconsistent |
834	| **Specstory** | macOS: brew tap → GitHub release fallback; Linux: GitHub release tarball | brew formula availability + version freshness |
835	| **CodexBar** | macOS: brew tap (arm64 only); Linux: Linuxbrew → GitHub release | arm64-specific package |
836	| **td** / **sidecar** | macOS: brew tap; Linux: Linuxbrew → GitHub release | same maintainer (`marcus/tap`); Linuxbrew is fast path when present |
837	| **Ollama** | brew formula always (CLI); brew cask `ollama-app` when `installAiDesktopApps + installLlmTools`; Linux: `curl ollama.com/install.sh` | CLI vs GUI split; vendor installer is the canonical Linux path |
838	| **fzf** | macOS: `lazyvim_deps` brew. Linux: chezmoi external + `~/.fzf/install --bin` | brew is fine on macOS; Linux gets the latest git tip |
839	| **bash** | system bash always; homebrew bash 5.x only when `primary_shell="bash"` on macOS | macOS ships bash 3.2 (GPL2 vintage); brew bash 5 needed only if user actually wants it as login shell |
840	| **gh** | macOS: brew (via `devtools`); Linux: vendor apt repo → user tarball fallback | brew is canonical macOS; vendor apt repo is canonical Linux |
841	| **tmux** | macOS: brew; Linux: apt → `nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage` when system < 3.3 | `display-menu` popup requires 3.3+ — see AGENTS.md tmux hard invariant |
842	| **Discord** | macOS: brew cask; Linux: flatpak (default) or `.deb` via `discordChannel` chooser | apt has no Discord; flatpak is sandboxed-and-current, `.deb` is for users who hate flatpak |
843	| **Steam** | macOS: brew cask gated by `installGamingApps`; Linux: Valve apt repo + `steam-launcher` gated by `installGamingApps` | Valve's apt repo is the supported Linux path; Flathub exists but is community-packaged |
844	| **just**, **starship**, **zoxide**, **direnv** | macOS: brew; Linux: vendor curl-installer | Linux distro packages are too stale for these fast-moving tools |
845	| **Neovim** | macOS: brew (`state: latest`); Linux: apt → GitHub release tarball → user fallback → `neovim/neovim-releases` on oldEL | Min version 0.11.2 is too new for most distros; no snap by policy |
846	| **tree-sitter-cli** | npm via mise (preferred, timeout 180) → cargo fallback | npm is faster; cargo needs libclang to compile. Same binary either way |
847	| **bw (Bitwarden CLI)** | npm global (preferred) or system npm fallback | always npm, the dispatch is mise-npm vs system-npm |
848	
849	**Adding a tool with multi-mechanism dispatch**: prefer ONE primary
850	mechanism per OS, with at most ONE fallback. Multiple fallbacks add
851	test combinations (5 levels × 5 OS variants = 25 cells) that nobody
852	will actually exercise. If you can't decide, write the simplest version
853	and add fallbacks only when an actual host fails.
854	
855	---
856	
857	## Fallback chains
858	
859	Notable cascading-fallback patterns:
860	
861	| Tool | Chain |
862	|---|---|
863	| **mise binary** | curl `https://mise.run` (preferred) → direct binary download from `mise.jdx.dev/mise-latest-linux-${arch}` → musl variant (forced when glibc < 2.28) |
864	| **Neovim (Linux)** | apt → GitHub release tarball when too old (`/opt/nvim` + symlink) → user-tarball to `~/.local` → `neovim-releases` fork (oldEL glibc 2.17 rebuild) |
865	| **Most Linux CLIs in base/devtools/networking_tools** | apt/yum (sudo) → user-level GitHub release musl tarball to `~/.local/bin`. Several have arch-specific brew-on-aarch64 branch (`eza`, `git-delta`) |
866	| **Rust (mise)** | configured mirror → official `static.rust-lang.org` → on oldEL: `rustup-init` directly |
867	| **Cursor `.deb` (Linux)** | `get_url` with retries=4 (large file, GFW-prone) — single mechanism but heavily retried |
868	| **Bitwarden Desktop (Linux)** | snap → `.deb` fallback |
869	| **CodexBar / td / sidecar / RTK / specstory / llmfit** | Linuxbrew → GitHub release tarball |
870	| **uv (upgrade-side)** | inspect binary path → `brew upgrade uv` or `uv self update` |
871	| **Discord (Linux)** | flatpak (default) → `.deb` (selectable via `discordChannel`) |
872	| **tree-sitter-cli (Linux)** | `mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` (timeout 180) → `cargo install tree-sitter-cli` (installs `libclang-dev` first) |
873	| **Antigravity installer** | curl → `sed` patch in-flight to inject `--skip-path --skip-aliases` → bash (avoids profile mutation) |
874	| **just** | macOS brew → Linux: vendor `curl install.sh` with `sudo` → user-level `--bin-dir ~/.local/bin` fallback |
875	
876	**Why fallbacks**: noRoot Linux hosts, RHEL/CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17, no
877	modern bottles, ancient zsh), Apple Silicon Macs (some brew formulae
878	have no arm64 bottle), Chinese-mirror outages.
879	
880	---
881	
882	## Coverage gaps (install-only, no automated upgrade)
883	
884	Tools that `chezmoi apply` installs but **no `upgrade_tools.sh` category
885	ever refreshes**. These tools stay frozen at install-time version until
886	manually removed and re-installed.
887	
888	| Class | Why no upgrade | How to refresh |
889	|---|---|---|
890	| **GitHub-release user-level fallbacks** (~30 tools — see [§ 11](#11-github-release-downloads-user-level-fallback)) | `creates:` guard means ansible never re-downloads | `rm ~/.local/bin/<tool>` then `chezmoi apply` |
891	| **Vendor apt-repo packages** on Debian (terraform, azure-cli, vscode, opentofu, ngrok, lazygit-from-PPA) | Rely on `sudo apt upgrade` outside this repo | `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade` (not chezmoi's job) |
892	| **Docker convenience-script install** | No upgrade target | re-run `curl get.docker.com \| sh` |
893	| **OrbStack** | Macos brew cask | Covered by `cat_brew --cask --greedy` |
894	| **Cursor `.deb`** / **Discord `.deb`** / **VSCode (Microsoft apt)** | apt-side, not chezmoi-side | apt-upgrade |
895	| **Zen Browser AppImage** / **AppImageLauncher Lite** | One-shot download, `creates:` guard | Delete AppImage, re-apply |
896	| **Hack Nerd Font** | `latest` URL, no version tracking | Delete font dir, re-apply |
897	| **fontconfig / libfuse2 / libnotify-bin / playerctl / wmctrl / xdotool** | System packages, no upgrade automation | apt-upgrade |
898	| **auditd rules** | Config files, not a "tool" with versions | Edit rule template, re-apply |
899	| **claude-hud / LazyVim plugins / TPM plugins / pre-commit / tldr cache / gh extensions** | **Covered** by `cat_plugins` in upgrade_tools.sh | `just upgrade-plugins` |
900	
901	**Why this matters**: a developer who runs `just upgrade-all` on a Linux
902	host gets brew + mise + uv + npm + cargo + dotnet + gem + flatpak +
903	agents + plugins moved forward. But ~30 GitHub-release-installed CLIs
904	(many of them widely-used: ripgrep, fd, jq, git-delta, lazygit, …)
905	stay pinned to install time forever. This is **partially mitigated**
906	by:
907	
908	- These tools on **macOS** all go via brew, which `cat_brew` covers
909	- On **Linux non-noRoot**, distro packages get apt-upgrade outside the repo
910	- The gap is sharpest on **noRoot Linux** where GitHub releases are
911	  the only install path AND there's no upgrade automation
912	
913	**Coverage gap on `cat_agents`**: only `claude / opencode / cursor-agent
914	/ ollama / llmfit / rtk / specstory` get the self-update-then-curl loop.
915	**Missing**: `agy` (Antigravity), `codexbar`, `td`, `sidecar`,
916	`specify-cli`, `openchamber`, `codex` — these rely on brew / uv / npm
917	categories instead.
918	
919	**Tracked on backlog**: no formal item yet, but adding a `releases`
920	category to `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` (audit installed binaries
921	against latest GitHub tag, prompt for refresh) would close this. See
922	[upgrades.md](upgrades.md#category-matrix) for the current category
923	list.
924

```text
1	# Linux GUI Apps — packaging mechanisms, this repo's strategy, and how to add a new one
2	
3	Ubuntu has **five** packaging mechanisms for desktop apps. They differ in
4	*where binaries land*, *whether anything keeps them current*, and *how
5	desktop integration (icon, `.desktop`, MIME handlers) gets wired up*.
6	
7	This doc:
8	
9	1. lays out the five mechanisms and the trade-off matrix,
10	2. inventories every GUI app this repo's `gui_apps_linux` ansible role
11	   knows about (plus the snaps you probably installed via Ubuntu App
12	   Center), so you can tell at a glance which path each app is on,
13	3. gives a decision tree for adding a *new* app to the role.
14	
15	## TL;DR — five mechanisms, one trade-off matrix
16	
17	| Mechanism | Auto-update? | Install scope | Desktop integration | Sandbox |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| **`.deb` w/ apt-source postinst** | ✅ via `apt upgrade` | system-wide (`/usr/share/...`) | ✅ baked in | ❌ |
20	| **`.deb` w/o apt-source postinst** | ❌ manual re-deploy | system-wide | ✅ baked in | ❌ |
21	| **Snap** (Ubuntu App Center) | ✅ `snapd` background daemon | `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` | ✅ baked in | ✅ confined |
22	| **Flatpak** (Flathub) | ✅ `flatpak update` | per-user `~/.var/app/...` | ✅ baked in | ✅ confined |
23	| **AppImage + AppImageLauncher** | ❌ re-download | per-user `~/Applications/` | ✅ via AIL daemon | ❌ |
24	| Cargo / from source | ❌ via `cargo install --force` | per-user `~/.cargo/bin/` | ❌ manual `.desktop` | ❌ |
25	| Tarball / `.tar.xz` | ❌ pure manual | per-user (anywhere) | ❌ manual | ❌ |
26	
27	The **green-checkmark `.deb` row is the gold standard** when upstream
28	provides it. Snap and Flatpak are the auto-update fallbacks for vendors
29	who don't ship `.deb` (or who want sandboxing). AppImage is the
30	last-mile bridge for everyone else.
31	
32	## Priority order on Ubuntu
33	
34	The matrix above is *what each mechanism does*. The list below is *which
35	to pick when you have a choice* — the explicit ordering this repo
36	follows when a vendor ships in multiple formats:
37	
38	1. **`.deb` w/ auto apt-source** — `apt upgrade` keeps it current with zero
39	   sandbox overhead and native startup speed. The right answer for
40	   hot-path apps (editors, terminals, browsers, daily-driver tools).
41	   Examples: Cursor, VSCode, Chrome, Signal, 1Password, Slack.
42	2. **Flatpak (Flathub)** — clean sandbox, cross-distro friendly, faster
43	   to launch than Snap, auto-update via `flatpak update`. Right when
44	   `.deb` is missing or vendor only publishes on Flathub. Default
45	   recommendation for community-packaged apps that need confinement.
46	3. **Snap** — set-and-forget auto-refresh via `snapd` (4×/day, no user
47	   action). Acceptable for non-hot-path apps where the extra ~1-3s
48	   startup penalty is invisible (password manager, music player).
49	   Avoid for hot-path apps; the daily startup cost adds up.
50	4. **AppImage + AppImageLauncher** — when 1-3 are unavailable. No
51	   auto-update unless the bundle ships `.zsync` AND AppImageLauncher's
52	   update check is configured. Re-running our ansible task is the
53	   typical refresh path.
54	5. **Cargo / from-source / tarball** — last resort. Manual everything,
55	   no apt/snap/flatpak update path. Only when upstream really only
56	   ships source.
57	
58	> **Why not "always Snap"?** Snap looks similar to Homebrew Cask on
59	> macOS but the comparison is misleading. Snap apps live in
60	> `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` mounted as squashfs and bring up an AppArmor
61	> sandbox on every launch — Firefox snap takes ~2-3s to boot on SSD
62	> versus ~0.3s for the `.deb`. The sandbox also breaks subtle workflows
63	> by default (snap Bitwarden can't read `~/.ssh` without `snap connect
64	> bitwarden:password-manager-service`; many snaps can't see external
65	> drives). For occasional-use apps these costs are invisible; for
66	> daily drivers (browser, IDE, terminal) they're a real annoyance.
67	> Snap is *fine* — it's just not the universal answer macOS users
68	> sometimes assume from their Cask experience. Pick by row 1-3 above.
69

109	
110	## Why `.deb` auto-update works (the apt-source postinst trick)
111	
112	When `dpkg -i cursor_<v>_amd64.deb` runs, Cursor's package contains a
113	`DEBIAN/postinst` script that, on success, writes:
114	
115	- `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources` — pointing at `https://downloads.cursor.com/aptrepo`
116	- `/usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg` — the signing key
117	
118	After that, `apt update` pulls Cursor's release index alongside Ubuntu's
119	own, and `apt upgrade cursor` (or generic `apt upgrade` / `just upgrade-system`)
120	treats it like any other apt package. The user never needs to revisit
121	cursor.com.
122	
123	You can verify this for any installed `.deb`:
124	
125	```sh
126	dpkg -L cursor | grep -E 'sources|keyring'
127	# /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cursor.sources
128	# /usr/share/keyrings/anysphere.gpg
129	```
130	
131	VSCode, Chrome, Signal, 1Password, Slack, Microsoft Edge, Brave all
132	follow this pattern. **Discord does not** — see the next section.
133	
134	## Discord auto-update — why the screenshot keeps appearing
135	
136	Discord's `.deb` does **not** ship a postinst that adds an apt source:
137	
138	```sh
139	dpkg -L discord | grep -E 'sources|keyring'
140	# (empty)
141	```
142	
143	So `apt upgrade` is never aware of new Discord releases. Discord's
144	in-app updater detects the version mismatch, but on Linux it can't
145	actually invoke `dpkg` (no root) — so it pops the *"Must be your lucky
146	day, there's a new update!"* modal with a "Download" button that just
147	opens the vendor download page. You then have to manually `dpkg -i` the
148	new `.deb`.
149	
150	Three ways out:
151	
152	1. **Re-run the ansible task on demand**: `chezmoi apply` (the role
153	   re-fetches the latest `.deb` URL via Discord's API every apply).
154	   This is what we do for Cursor too, so it's consistent.
155	2. **Switch to Flatpak**: `flatpak install flathub com.discordapp.Discord`.
156	   Flatpak auto-updates via `flatpak update`. Loses some native
157	   integration (notifications via XDG portal, screen-share via
158	   PipeWire) but the upgrade story is clean.
159	3. **Switch to Vesktop / WebCord** (community Discord clients with
160	   self-update). Drift from official Discord; not recommended unless
161	   you're already running modded Discord.
162	
163	**This repo's default is option 2 (Flatpak)** — controlled by the
164	`discordChannel` chezmoi prompt (`flatpak | deb | none`, default `flatpak`).
165	The role's flatpak path:
166	
167	1. apt-installs the `flatpak` package if missing (one-time, with sudo)
168	2. adds the Flathub remote at user scope (no sudo)
169	3. installs `com.discordapp.Discord` at user scope (no sudo)
170	
171	To switch from `.deb` to `flatpak` on an existing machine: set
172	`discordChannel = "flatpak"` in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` and run
173	`chezmoi apply --tags gui_apps`. The two installs can coexist briefly
174	(different `.desktop` entries); once you've validated the Flatpak version,
175	`sudo apt remove discord` to clean up the old `.deb`.
176	
177	## Steam — why this uses Valve's apt repo, not Flatpak/Snap
178	
179	Steam is gated by `installGamingApps=true` and currently only installed on
180	x86_64 Ubuntu Desktop. Valve publishes an official apt repository at
181	`https://repo.steampowered.com/steam/`; the role installs its signing key
182	from `archive/stable/steam.gpg`, enables `i386`, adds the repo as deb822,
183	and installs `steam-launcher`.
184	
185	The `i386` architecture is intentional: Steam still needs 32-bit runtime
186	libraries for parts of the launcher and many games. Do not hard-code old
187	Mesa package names from older guides (for example `libgl1-mesa-glx`) in the
188	role; Ubuntu 24.04 no longer ships that package. Let `steam-launcher` pull
189	the current dependencies and recommends.
190	
191	Flathub's `com.valvesoftware.Steam` exists, but it is a community package
192	and explicitly not Valve's supported path. It also needs extra filesystem
193	overrides for libraries on non-default drives. If this repo ever adds a
194	`steamChannel` prompt, keep Valve apt as the default.
195	
196	## Snap (Ubuntu App Center) — what's actually happening
197	
198	The Ubuntu App Center is a GTK frontend for `snapd` — Canonical's
199	universal package manager that ships `.snap` archives from the Snap
200	Store. When you install **Bitwarden** or **Spotify** from App Center:
201	
202	- The `.snap` file is extracted to `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` (versioned,
203	  read-only)
204	- A symlink `/snap/<app>/current` always points at the active rev
205	- A wrapper script at `/snap/bin/<app>` is what `$PATH` actually picks up
206	- A user-systemd service `snapd.refresh.service` checks for updates
207	  ~4× per day and applies them in the background
208	- Desktop integration (`/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications/<app>.desktop`)
209	  is auto-generated; the snap-store daemon updates these on refresh
210	
211	This means **Bitwarden Desktop and Spotify will keep themselves up to
212	date with no manual action** — the same way `apt upgrade` doesn't run
213	automatically but apt-source `.deb`s are kept current via your existing
214	`just upgrade-system` cadence, snaps are kept current via `snapd`'s
215	*always-on* refresh daemon. Different paradigm, same end result.
216	
217	To inspect: `snap list`, `snap info <app>`, `snap refresh --list`
218	(pending updates), `snap refresh <app>` (force-refresh now), `snap
219	revert <app>` (rollback to previous rev — neat property of the
220	versioned `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` layout).
221	
222	> Caveat: snaps run in a confinement sandbox, which can break power-user
223	> workflows (no access to `~/.ssh` by default for example). Most desktop
224	> apps work fine; CLI tools sometimes don't. Prefer `.deb` or apt
225	> when both options exist.
226	
227	## AppImage + AppImageLauncher — the catch-all
228	
229	When upstream ships only an AppImage (Zen Browser, Cursor's old AppImage,
230	many indie tools), our convention is:
231	
232	1. **Stable filename**: drop the file at `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage`
233	   (no version or hash in the name). Re-runs of the ansible task just
234	   overwrite it. Files like `zen-x86_64_fe71259e...AppImage` (old hash
235	   suffix in filename) are the wrong shape — they accumulate forever.
236	2. **Executable bit**: `mode: '0755'` in the ansible task.
237	3. **AppImageLauncher integration**: `appimagelauncherd.service` (user
238	   systemd unit, set up by our role) watches `~/Applications/`. New
239	   AppImages trigger a first-run modal: *"Integrate or Run once?"* —
240	   integrating extracts the icon, generates a `.desktop` entry under
241	   `~/.local/share/applications/`, and (optionally) moves the file to
242	   AppImageLauncher's canonical location.
243	
244	For our managed AppImages we usually skip the modal by writing the
245	`.desktop` entry ourselves in the same ansible task — see Zen Browser.
246	For AppImages you drop manually (Frpc Desktop), let the modal handle it.
247	
248	To check the daemon: `systemctl --user status appimagelauncherd`.
249	Manual integration: `ail-cli integrate ~/Applications/foo.AppImage`.
250	
251	## Adding a new GUI app to `gui_apps_linux`
252	
253	```
254	Does upstream publish a .deb?
255	├─ YES → Does the .deb add an apt source (check `dpkg -L <pkg> | grep sources` after install)?
256	│        ├─ YES → use the .deb. Ansible installs once, apt keeps current. ★ best path
257	│        └─ NO  → use the .deb anyway, BUT add a refresh hook to
258	│                 `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` so `just upgrade-system`
259	│                 re-fetches latest. (Discord pattern.)
260	│
261	├─ NO ── Does upstream publish on Snap or Flatpak with FIRST-PARTY support?
262	│        ├─ Official Snap → use snap (community.general.snap module).
263	│        │                 Cleanest auto-update on Ubuntu, but confined.
264	│        ├─ Official Flathub → use flatpak (community.general.flatpak module).
265	│        │                    Cross-distro friendly, also confined.
266	│        └─ Community-only → skip; AppImage probably more reliable.
267	│
268	└─ Only AppImage / tarball?
269	   ├─ AppImage → drop in ~/Applications/ as <app>.AppImage. AIL integrates.
270	   └─ tarball  → ~/Applications/<app>/ + wrapper script + manual .desktop.
271	                 ⚠️ Last resort — no auto-update path, manual everything.
272	```
273	
274	### Concrete patterns
275	
276	**`.deb` pattern** — see "Install Cursor via .deb" in
277	[`gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml).
278	Two-step:
279	
280	1. `ansible.builtin.uri` — fetch vendor's API to resolve the latest
281	   `.deb` URL (return JSON, parse `debUrl` or similar field).
282	2. `ansible.builtin.get_url` — download the `.deb`, with `force: true`
283	   (overwrite stale files from prior apply) and `until: cursor_dl is
284	   succeeded` + `retries: 4` + `delay: 5` (GFW-region CDN drops).
285	3. `ansible.builtin.apt: deb=<path>` — install. Postinst handles apt
286	   source if vendor ships one.
287	4. Wrap the whole block in `rescue:` that prints a manual-fallback URL.
288	
289	**AppImage pattern** — see "Install Zen Browser AppImage" in the same
290	file. Three-step:
291	
292	1. `ansible.builtin.uri` — GitHub releases API (or vendor equivalent)
293	   to resolve the asset URL.
294	2. `selectattr('name', 'match', '^<prefix>-<arch>\\.AppImage$')` filter
295	   to pick the right asset for `target_architecture` (already normalized
296	   to `x86_64` / `aarch64` by the `Set target_architecture from dpkg` task
297	   in [`linux.yml`](../../dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml)).
298	3. `ansible.builtin.get_url` to `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage` with
299	   `mode: '0755'` and a stable filename.
300	4. Write a `.desktop` entry under `~/.local/share/applications/` using
301	   `ansible.builtin.copy` with a `content:` literal — the file gets
302	   merged into the system menu via `update-desktop-database`.
303	
304	**Snap pattern** — none yet in this repo. Template:
305	
306	```yaml
307	- name: Install Bitwarden Desktop via Snap
308	  community.general.snap:
309	    name: bitwarden
310	    state: present
311	    classic: false   # most apps are confined; set true only when vendor docs say so
312	  become: true
313	```
314	
315	**Flatpak pattern** — none yet. Template:
316	
317	```yaml
318	- name: Install Discord via Flatpak (instead of .deb)
319	  community.general.flatpak:
320	    name: com.discordapp.Discord
321	    state: present
322	    remote: flathub  # add `community.general.flatpak_remote` first if missing
323	    method: user     # per-user install; `system` requires root
324	```
325	
326	Always add a `rescue:` block that points the user at the manual
327	fallback URL (cursor.com / discord.com / GitHub release page) so a
328	failed automated install isn't a dead end.
329	
330	## Controlling installed apps from the shell
331	
332	The role installs apps; `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` controls
333	them. Linux counterpart to the macOS `app-*` helpers in
334	`dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` — **same public function names**
335	(`appquit` / `applaunch` / `appactivate` / `apprestart` / `apprunning` /
336	`applist` / `appresponsive`) so users get cross-platform muscle memory.
337	The `tv linux-apps` channel mirrors `tv mac-apps`.
338	
339	### Coverage on Wayland GNOME (no compositor extension)
340	
341	| Verb | Linux backend | Fidelity |
342	|---|---|---|
343	| `applaunch NAME` | `gtk-launch <desktop-id>` (no `DBusActivatable=true` required) | ✓ works for any `.desktop` file |
344	| `apprunning NAME` | `pgrep -f <pattern>` (override or auto-derived) | ✓ silent boolean |
345	| `appquit NAME` | `pkill -TERM -f <pattern>` | ✓ Electron + Firefox quit gracefully on SIGTERM |
346	| `apprestart NAME` | quit + poll-gone (≤15s) + launch | ✓ launches even if not running |
347	| `appactivate NAME` | D-Bus → GNOME `window-calls` ext; fallback `gtk-launch` | ⚠ full focus only with extension installed |
348	| `applist [--pids\|--all]` | registry + `.desktop` scan, pgrep each | ⚠ "managed apps that are alive" — not every window |
349	| `appresponsive NAME [T]` | `playerctl -p <mpris>` for media apps; degrades to `apprunning` | ⚠ MPRIS-only; no Linux analog to macOS Apple Events |
350	
351	### Why `gapplication` alone doesn't work
352	
353	The freedesktop `org.freedesktop.Application` D-Bus interface is the
354	semantic match to macOS Apple Events — apps expose `quit` / `activate` /
355	etc. and `gapplication action <id> quit` calls them. **In practice, almost
356	no third-party app sets `DBusActivatable=true` in its `.desktop` file**:
357	empirically, on a daily-driver Ubuntu 24.04 Wayland session,
358	`gapplication list-apps` returned 13 entries — *all GNOME-core* (Calendar,
359	Logs, Nautilus, …). Zero of the user's Zen / Cursor / Spotify / Discord /
360	Frpc-Desktop showed up. See
361	[`pitfalls/linux-app-control-gapplication-zero-coverage.md`](../../pitfalls/linux-app-control-gapplication-zero-coverage.md).
362	
363	Hybrid pivot: launch via `gtk-launch` (works for any `.desktop` file
364	regardless of `DBusActivatable`); quit via `pkill -TERM` on a runtime
365	pattern; focus via the optional `window-calls` GNOME extension.
366	
367	### Override file: `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf`
368	
369	Not auto-stubbed (mirrors `~/.shellrc.secrets` rule — empty-file footgun).
370	Helper sources it if present. Register apps with `linux_app_register`:
371	
372	```sh
373	# Cursor — apt install at /usr/share/cursor/cursor (NOT the AppImage residue)
374	linux_app_register Cursor \
375	  --desktop=cursor \
376	  --pkill='^/usr/share/cursor/cursor( |$)' \
377	  --wm-class=Cursor
378	
379	# Discord — apt install; ignore the Flatpak duplicate
380	linux_app_register Discord \
381	  --desktop=discord \
382	  --pkill='^/usr/share/discord/Discord( |$)' \
383	  --wm-class=discord
384	
385	# Spotify — snap-confined, MPRIS-aware
386	linux_app_register Spotify \
387	  --desktop=spotify_spotify \
388	  --pkill='^/snap/spotify/[^/]+/usr/share/spotify/spotify' \
389	  --wm-class=spotify \
390	  --mpris=spotify
391	
392	# Zen Browser — AppImage, runtime path != .desktop Exec
393	linux_app_register Zen \
394	  --desktop=zen-browser \
395	  --pkill='\.mount_.+/zen($| )' \
396	  --wm-class=zen
397	
398	# Frpc-Desktop — AppImage, runtime path drifts on re-download
399	linux_app_register Frpc-Desktop \
400	  --desktop=appimagekit_557220393761292184db845cd26816c3-Frpc-Desktop \
401	  --pkill='\.mount_.+/frpc-desktop($| )' \
402	  --wm-class=Frpc-Desktop
403	
404	# ClashForWindows — manually-placed Electron app, NO .desktop file.
405	# Use --exec= for the launch path; helper prefers --exec over --desktop.
406	linux_app_register CFW \
407	  --exec='~/Documents/ClashForWindows/cfw' \
408	  --pkill='^/home/.+/Documents/ClashForWindows/cfw' \
409	  --wm-class='Clash for Windows'
410	```
411	
412	The `--exec=` flag covers apps with no `.desktop` (manually-placed
413	Electron / hand-built binaries). The flag value is passed through `eval`
414	to expand `~` and `$HOME`, and is executed via `setsid -f sh -c …` so
415	the parent shell stays clean.
416	
417	`linux_app_register --list` prints the current registry; `--help` prints
418	flag reference.
419	
420	**When to override vs let auto-derivation handle it**:
421	
422	- **Always override** for AppImage, Snap, and Flatpak apps. AppImage
423	  runtime binary lives at `/tmp/.mount_<hash>/<inner>`, not the
424	  `.desktop` `Exec=` path — `pkill` on the `Exec=` path only hits the
425	  launcher wrapper. See
426	  [`pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md`](../../pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md).
427	- **Override when an app has multiple `.desktop` entries** (Zen with 4
428	  AppImage residues, Cursor with AppImage residue + apt install, Discord
429	  with apt + Flatpak both installed). Auto-derivation picks latest
430	  mtime, which may not be the one that's actually running.
431	- **Skip override** for clean apt-installed apps (their `Exec=` matches
432	  the runtime path 1:1) — auto-derivation handles them correctly.
433	
434	### GNOME `window-calls` extension — manual install
435	
436	The helper detects the extension at first `appactivate` call. Without it,
437	`appactivate` falls back to `applaunch`, which re-focuses for
438	single-instance apps like Electron + Firefox but isn't reliable for all
439	apps. Install once per host:
440	
441	```sh
442	# Download from GitHub releases or extensions.gnome.org
443	# https://github.com/ickyicky/window-calls (or hseliger/window-calls-extended
444	# for GNOME 45+ if upstream is stale)
445	gnome-extensions install ~/Downloads/window-calls@domandoman.xyz.zip
446	gnome-extensions enable window-calls@domandoman.xyz
447	```
448	
449	**Wayland sessions need a logout + login** for the extension to activate
450	(no `Alt+F2 r` reload like X11). The user-consent dialog on GNOME 46+
451	can't be suppressed, so this isn't ansible-automatable.
452	
453	### Known limits (mirror the backlog)
454	
455	- **No analog to macOS Apple Events' `with timeout`** for non-MPRIS apps.
456	  `appresponsive` for Electron / Firefox / native GTK apps degrades to
457	  `apprunning` with a stderr note.
458	- **No "hide windows" verb** (mac-apps Alt+H has no Linux equivalent
459	  without compositor IPC; deliberately omitted from `tv linux-apps`).
460	- **`applist` is "registered + auto-derived running apps"**, not "every
461	  GUI window". Auto-discovery filters to `.desktop` entries whose `Exec=`
462	  is an absolute path (skips Flatpak/AppImage wrappers that would match
463	  too loosely).
464	- **Compositor support is GNOME Wayland only.** KDE / Sway / Hyprland
465	  paths aren't wired — see `backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md` for
466	  the deferred matrix if a second compositor joins the fleet.
467	
468	## Cross-references
469	
470	- [`docs/tools/appimage.md`](../tools/appimage.md) — AppImageLauncher install paths, `ail-cli`, libfuse2 / AppArmor gotchas on Ubuntu 24.04.
471	- [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](../this_repo/upgrades.md) — the install-vs-upgrade split: why `chezmoi apply` doesn't bump versions, what `just upgrade-*` covers, where each package manager fits in.
472	- [`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) — the actual ansible role, with the patterns you'd copy when adding a new app.
473	- [`backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md`](../../backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md) — design history for the `app-*` helpers, options considered, and deferred follow-ups (KDE / Sway / Hyprland).
474
```

1	---
2	# Linux playbook - Ubuntu/Debian setup
3	- name: Linux setup
4	  hosts: local
5	  gather_facts: true
6	
7	  pre_tasks:
8	    # RPi 4 can run a 64-bit kernel (aarch64) with 32-bit userland (armhf).
9	    # ansible_facts['architecture'] reflects the kernel, which leads to
10	    # downloading aarch64 binaries that cannot execute.  Detect the real
11	    # userland architecture and expose it as target_architecture for all roles.
12	    # Note: set_fact cannot reliably override ansible_facts['architecture']
13	    # when inject_facts_as_vars=False, so we use a dedicated variable instead.
14	    - name: Detect userland architecture via dpkg
15	      ansible.builtin.command: dpkg --print-architecture
16	      register: dpkg_arch_result
17	      changed_when: false
18	      failed_when: false
19	      tags: [always]
20	
21	    - name: Set target_architecture from dpkg
22	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
23	        target_architecture: >-
24	          {{ {'amd64': 'x86_64', 'arm64': 'aarch64', 'armhf': 'armv7l', 'armel': 'armv6l', 'i386': 'i686'}
25	             [dpkg_arch_result.stdout | trim]
26	             | default(ansible_facts['architecture']) }}
27	      when: dpkg_arch_result.rc == 0 and dpkg_arch_result.stdout | trim != ''
28	      tags: [always]
29	
30	    - name: Fallback target_architecture to gathered facts
31	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
32	        target_architecture: "{{ ansible_facts['architecture'] }}"
33	      when: target_architecture is not defined

182	## What You Get
183	
184	### Config Files
185	
186	- `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration; managed via `modify_` so `gh auth setup-git`'s `[credential "..."]` blocks (with the per-machine absolute path to `gh`) survive `chezmoi apply`; default pull behavior is rebase + autostash (`pull.rebase=true`, `rebase.autoStash=true`) so LazyGit's `p` pull keeps local dirty work across the rebase ([docs](docs/tools/gh-cli.md), [LazyGit notes](docs/tools/lazygit.md))
187	- `~/.config/git/hooks/` - Global Git hooks (via a global `core.hooksPath`): managed `pre-commit` (gitleaks) + Git LFS hooks, all hardened to skip gracefully — PATH-robust and non-fatal so a stripped-PATH clone like `brew tap` can't break (see [pitfall](pitfalls/git-lfs-global-hook-breaks-brew-tap.md))
188	- `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml` - Global gh-dash config, with `diffnav` as the diff pager
189	- `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` - Global LazyGit config, with `delta` as the custom diff pager
190	- `~/.config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme` - Managed Tokyo Night theme for bat; apply rebuilds the bat cache and clears it if the cache is incompatible with `delta`
191	- `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration; system clipboard via `unnamedplus`, with an SSH-conditional OSC 52 override so remote yanks reach the local clipboard (pairs with tmux `set-clipboard on`, see [docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md#osc-52-clipboard-ssh-friendly-yank))
192	- `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config (PyPI: official / Aliyun+TUNA+USTC via `useChineseMirror`)
193	- `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry config (crates.io / TUNA sparse index via `useChineseMirror`)
194	- `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
195	- `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
196	- `~/.gemrc` - RubyGems source + common options (TUNA mirror; only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, gated via `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`)
197	- `~/.condarc` - Conda/Mamba channels with TUNA Anaconda mirror (only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, preserves `auto_activate_base`/user channel prefs)
198	- `~/.config/zsh/00_exports.zsh` - Env-var mirror bundle (Homebrew / Rustup / mise / GOPROXY) when `useChineseMirror=true`; also exported by bootstrap + ansible runner scripts so first-run installs and ansible subprocesses inherit them ([docs](docs/tools/mirrors.md))
199	- `~/.config/zsh/99_local_proxy.zsh` - Create-only machine-local proxy override stub; uncomment `LOCAL_PROXY_URL` / `LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` here to pin Clash ports without future chezmoi diffs
200	- `~/.docker/config.json` - Docker client `proxies.default` block (auto-injected from `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` / `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL`; preserves `auths` / `credsStore` via chezmoi modify-script) ([docs](docs/tools/containers.md))
201	- `~/.config/docker/daemon.json` - Rootless Docker `registry-mirrors` (DaoCloud / USTC / NJU / ...; Linux + `useChineseMirror` only) ([docs](docs/tools/containers.md#strategy-a-registry-mirrors-in-daemonjson))
202	- `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config (CSI-u keybindings for `Ctrl+Number` tmux window switching, `option_as_alt` for Meta keys)
203	- `~/Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (macOS) + `~/.config/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (Linux) - Editor settings overlay: `modify_settings.json` deep-merges a 6-key baseline (Hack Nerd Font Mono, relative line numbers, format on save, smart-accept suggestion, terminal font) into each editor's live `settings.json` without overwriting other keys; `create_keybindings.json` seeds 5 universal keybindings on a fresh machine and never overwrites editor-added entries. Canonical templates live under [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`](.chezmoitemplates/editor/); `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` gates each editor dir with a `stat` presence check so uninstalled editors never produce phantom directories.
204	- `~/.config/ghostty/config` - Ghostty/cmux terminal config (`macos-option-as-alt` for tmux Meta keybindings, disabled ligatures, explicit `clipboard-write = allow` / `clipboard-read = ask` for OSC 52) ([docs](docs/tools/ghostty.md))
205	- `~/.config/starship.toml` - Starship cross-shell prompt config
206	- `~/.xonshrc` + `~/.config/xonsh/rc.xsh` - Optional [Xonsh](https://xon.sh/) (Python-superset shell) startup + extension sandbox. Installed via `python_uv_tools` with a curated set of xontribs (`jedi`/`zoxide`/`pipeliner`/`fzf-widgets`); **not** a login shell — drop in with `xonsh` for ad-hoc Python-in-shell work ([docs](docs/shells/xonsh.md))
207	- `~/.config/direnv/direnvrc` - direnv helper functions, including `.venv`-aware Python activation
208	- `~/.config/yazi/` - Yazi file manager config (v0.3.3+ syntax, [docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/overview/))

303	            fi
304	        fi
305	    done

319	# Run brew bundle up to N times. Subsequent attempts only retry items that
320	# failed (already-installed packages are skipped quickly). This papers over
321	# transient GitHub CDN / HTTP/2 errors that commonly hit large cask lists.
322	# Between attempts we wipe Homebrew's `.incomplete*` lockfiles so a previously
323	# interrupted parallel `brew fetch` doesn't poison the retry with
324	# "process has already locked ... .incomplete" errors.
325	BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS="${BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS:-2}"
326	clear_brew_download_locks() {
327	    local cache_dir
328	    cache_dir="$(brew --cache 2>/dev/null)/downloads"
329	    [[ -d "$cache_dir" ]] || return 0
330	    # Both .incomplete data files and their .lock siblings.
331	    find "$cache_dir" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.incomplete*' -print -delete 2>/dev/null \
332	        | head -20 \
333	        | while IFS= read -r f; do info "  cleared stale lock: $(basename "$f")"; done
334	}
335	
336	trust_bundle_taps() {
337	    local file="$1"
338	    local taps tap info_out
339	    [[ -f "$file" ]] || return 0
340	    taps="$(brew bundle list --taps --file="$file" 2>/dev/null || true)"
341	    [[ -n "$taps" ]] || return 0
342	
343	    while IFS= read -r tap; do
344	        [[ -n "$tap" ]] || continue
345	        if ! brew tap | grep -qFx -- "$tap"; then
346	            if ! brew tap "$tap"; then
347	                warn "Could not tap $tap before brew bundle; brew bundle will retry normally"
348	                continue
349	            fi
350	        fi
351	
352	        info_out="$(brew tap-info "$tap" 2>/dev/null || true)"
353	        if [[ "$info_out" == *Untrusted* ]]; then
354	            info "Trusting Homebrew tap $tap"
355	            brew trust "$tap"
356	        fi
357	    done <<< "$taps"
358	}
359	
360	run_bundle_with_retry() {
361	    local file="$1"
362	    local label="$2"
363	    local attempt=1
364	    while (( attempt <= BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS )); do
365	        if (( attempt == 1 )); then
366	            info "Installing $label..."
367	        else
368	            info "Retrying $label (attempt $attempt/$BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS, only missing items)..."
369	            clear_brew_download_locks
370	        fi
371	        trust_bundle_taps "$file"

373	            return 0
374	        fi
375	        attempt=$(( attempt + 1 ))
376	    done
377	    warn "Some packages in $label still failed after $BUNDLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS attempts (continuing...)"

379	    return 0
380	}

135	# ansible-core 2.18+ modules wrap themselves in `from __future__ import
136	# annotations` (Py3.7+ syntax). When ansible runs against a target whose
137	# auto-discovered `/usr/bin/python3` is older (CentOS 7 ships 3.6.8),

139	#   SyntaxError: future feature annotations is not defined

141	# Detect the auto-discovered python's version; if < 3.7, fall back to
142	# uv's managed python (already pulled into ~/.local/share/uv/python/...
143	# by `uv tool install ansible-core` in bootstrap) and pass it via
144	# -e ansible_python_interpreter. This is forward-compatible: on Rocky 9
145	# (Py 3.9+) the override is unnecessary and the if-branch is skipped.
146	#

148	# matching controller-side fix; this is the target-side companion.

150	detect_target_python() {
151	    local sys_py="${1:-/usr/bin/python3}"
152	    if ! [[ -x "$sys_py" ]]; then
153	        return 1
154	    fi
155	    local sys_ver
156	    sys_ver="$("$sys_py" -c 'import sys; print(f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}")' 2>/dev/null)" || return 1

158	    awk -v v="$sys_ver" 'BEGIN { split(v, a, "."); exit !(a[1]>3 || (a[1]==3 && a[2]>=7)) }'

165	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
166	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.11.*-linux-*/bin/python3 \
167	                "$HOME"/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.10.*-linux-*/bin/python3; do
168	        if [[ -x "$cand" ]]; then

Never hand-edit the generated marker regions. | `just gen-prompts -- --check` / the `dotfiles-init-gen-check` pre-commit hook fail on drift; `doctor` is a back-compat alias for `gen --check`. |

The PATH-augmentation prelude in `scripts/fleet/pueue.py:_REMOTE_CMD` and `scripts/fleet/exec.py:_PATH_PRELUDE` MUST stay in sync — both rely on the same chezmoi → cargo → uv → ~/bin → brew → linuxbrew order (deliberately diverges from the user's interactive shell PATH so package-manager dirs win over legacy ~/bin). |

**Three-tier file placement** for new shell helpers:

| Tier | Dir | When |
|---|---|---|
| Shared | `dot_config/shell/` | POSIX subset, both shells source. `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION` source-time dispatch is OK; ZLE widgets / `compdef` / `bindkey` / `setopt` / `read -q` / `${m:t}` / glob qualifiers are NOT (bash would error on source). |
| Zsh-only | `dot_config/zsh/` | ZLE widgets, `compdef`, `bindkey`, `setopt`, zsh-vi-mode hooks. |
| Bash-only | `dot_config/bash/` | `bind -x` / `ble-bind`, OMB plugin arrays, bash-specific `shopt`s. |

When porting a zsh-only helper to bash via ble.sh, extract the shell-agnostic backend into `dot_config/shell/` and keep each shell's widget binding in its own dir.

### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files

Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):

1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers

**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.

  sudo apt update
  sudo apt install resilio-sync

- Enable at boot:

87	  become: true
88	  tags: [sudo]
89	  ansible.builtin.shell: >-
90	    set -o pipefail;
91	    dmidecode -t 38 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'IPMI Device Information' || true
92	  args:
93	    executable: /bin/bash
94	  register: homelab_ipmi_dmi
95	  changed_when: false
96	  failed_when: false
97	  check_mode: false   # read-only probe; must run even during --check
98	
99	- name: Consolidate hardware-presence facts
100	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
101	    homelab_has_raid: "{{ (homelab_raid_probe.stdout | default('') | trim) | length > 0 }}"
102	    homelab_has_nvme: "{{ (homelab_nvme_probe.stdout | default('') | trim) | length > 0 }}"
103	    homelab_has_bmc: >-
104	      {{ (homelab_ipmi_dev.matched | default(0) | int > 0)
105	         or ((homelab_ipmi_dmi.stdout | default('') | trim) | length > 0) }}
106	
107	- name: Show detected hardware
108	  ansible.builtin.debug:
109	    msg: >-
110	      homelab_tools detection — RAID controller: {{ homelab_has_raid }},
111	      NVMe: {{ homelab_has_nvme }}, BMC/IPMI: {{ homelab_has_bmc }}
112	
113	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	# Always-useful installs on physical Linux (sensors + SMART work everywhere)
115	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
116	
117	- name: Build base package list (lm-sensors + smartmontools)
118	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
119	    homelab_pkgs: >-
120	      {{ (([('lm-sensors' if ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian' else 'lm_sensors')]
121	            if homelab_install_lm_sensors else [])
122	          + (['smartmontools'] if homelab_install_smartmontools else [])
123	          + (['ipmitool'] if (homelab_install_ipmitool and homelab_has_bmc) else [])
124	          + (['nvme-cli'] if (homelab_install_nvme_cli and homelab_has_nvme) else [])) }}
125	
126	- name: Install homelab hardware tools (Debian / Ubuntu)
127	  when:
128	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
129	    - homelab_pkgs | length > 0
130	  become: true
131	  tags: [sudo]
132	  ansible.builtin.apt:
133	    name: "{{ homelab_pkgs }}"
134	    state: present
135	    # Main-archive packages covered by base's best-effort cache refresh; don't
136	    # re-run apt-get update here (a broken/flaky source would abort the play).
137	    # See pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md.
138	    update_cache: false
139	
140	- name: Install homelab hardware tools (RHEL / CentOS / Rocky / Alma)
141	  when:
142	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
143	    - homelab_pkgs | length > 0
144	  become: true
145	  tags: [sudo]
146	  ansible.builtin.yum:
147	    name: "{{ homelab_pkgs }}"
148	    state: present
149	
150	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
151	# storcli — only when a RAID controller is present. Not in distro repos, so
152	# this is a best-effort vendor/mirror download gated on `homelab_storcli_url`.
153	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
154	
155	- name: Check whether storcli is already installed
156	  when: homelab_install_storcli and homelab_has_raid
157	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v storcli || command -v storcli64 || true
158	  args:
159	    executable: /bin/bash
160	  register: homelab_storcli_check
161	  changed_when: false
162	  failed_when: false
163	  check_mode: false   # read-only probe; must run even during --check
164	
165	- name: Install storcli from vendor URL (RAID present, not installed, URL set)
166	  when:
167	    - homelab_install_storcli
168	    - homelab_has_raid
169	    - (homelab_storcli_check.stdout | default('') | trim) | length == 0
170	    - homelab_storcli_url | length > 0
171	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
172	  block:
173	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (storcli)
174	      ansible.builtin.file:
175	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
176	        state: directory
177	        mode: "0755"
178	
179	    - name: Download storcli archive
180	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
181	        url: "{{ homelab_storcli_url }}"
182	        dest: /tmp/storcli_dl
183	        mode: "0644"
184	        timeout: 120
185	      retries: 3
186	      delay: 5
187	
188	    - name: Create storcli extract directory
189	      ansible.builtin.file:
190	        path: /tmp/storcli_extract
191	        state: directory
192	        mode: "0755"
193	
194	    - name: Extract storcli archive
195	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
196	        src: /tmp/storcli_dl
197	        dest: /tmp/storcli_extract
198	        remote_src: true
199	
200	    - name: Find storcli binary in extracted tree
201	      ansible.builtin.find:
202	        paths: /tmp/storcli_extract
203	        patterns: "storcli,storcli64"
204	        file_type: file
205	        recurse: true
206	      register: homelab_storcli_find
207	
208	    - name: Fail if storcli binary not found after extraction
209	      when: homelab_storcli_find.matched | default(0) | int == 0
210	      ansible.builtin.fail:
211	        msg: "storcli binary not found under /tmp/storcli_extract — check homelab_storcli_url"
212	
213	    - name: Install storcli to ~/.local/bin
214	      ansible.builtin.copy:
215	        src: "{{ homelab_storcli_find.files[0].path }}"
216	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/storcli"
217	        mode: "0755"
218	        remote_src: true
219	  rescue:
220	    - name: Warn storcli install failed
221	      ansible.builtin.debug:
222	        msg: >-
223	          storcli install failed — skipping. Install manually (see
224	          docs/sysadmin/hardware.md "Installing storcli").
225	          Error: {{ ansible_failed_result.msg | default('unknown') }}
226	  always:
227	    - name: Clean up storcli temp files
228	      ansible.builtin.file:
229	        path: "{{ item }}"
230	        state: absent
231	      loop:
232	        - /tmp/storcli_dl
233	        - /tmp/storcli_extract
234	
235	- name: Hint when RAID present but storcli unavailable and no URL configured
236	  when:
237	    - homelab_install_storcli
238	    - homelab_has_raid
239	    - (homelab_storcli_check.stdout | default('') | trim) | length == 0
240	    - homelab_storcli_url | length == 0
241	  ansible.builtin.debug:
242	    msg: >-
243	      A RAID controller was detected but storcli is not installed and
244	      homelab_storcli_url is empty. Set that var to a reachable storcli tarball,
245	      or install manually — see docs/sysadmin/hardware.md "Installing storcli".
246	
247	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
248	# Note: smartd / ipmievd services are intentionally NOT enabled. This repo is
249	# install-only (see CLAUDE.md "Install vs upgrade is split on purpose"); a
250	# monitoring/alerting timer would be a separate opt-in feature.
251

184	    - { src: "resources/niri-shutdown.target", dest: "/etc/systemd/user/niri-shutdown.target", mode: "0644" }

186	# --- Desktop usability: launcher --------------------------------------------
187	# niri boots to an empty screen; a launcher (Mod+D) is the minimum to not get
188	# stuck. fuzzel is the launcher referenced in config.kdl.
189	#
190	# The Mod+T terminal is alacritty, cargo-built by gui_apps_linux into
191	# ~/.cargo/bin — which is NOT on the GDM/systemd graphical-session PATH. That's
192	# fixed PER-USER in config.kdl's `environment { PATH … }` block (chezmoi
193	# templates the user's own $HOME in), NOT a system-wide /usr/local/bin symlink:
194	# a shared system path pointing into one user's $HOME breaks on multi-user
195	# hosts (permission-denied traversing $HOME, dangling link if that user rebuilds,
196	# and a non-root user controlling a system-PATH binary). So nothing
197	# alacritty-related happens here.
198	# (Zen/VSCode/Cursor/Discord need neither: AppImage abs-paths or /usr/bin.)
199	
200	- name: Install fuzzel (Mod+D app launcher)
201	  when:
202	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
203	    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
204	    - not (niri_no_root | default(false) | bool)
205	  become: true
206	  tags: [sudo]
207	  ansible.builtin.apt:
208	    name: fuzzel
209	    state: present

256	│        ├─ YES → use the .deb. Ansible installs once, apt keeps current. ★ best path
257	│        └─ NO  → use the .deb anyway, BUT add a refresh hook to
258	│                 `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` so `just upgrade-system`
259	│                 re-fetches latest. (Discord pattern.)
260	│
261	├─ NO ── Does upstream publish on Snap or Flatpak with FIRST-PARTY support?
262	│        ├─ Official Snap → use snap (community.general.snap module).
263	│        │                 Cleanest auto-update on Ubuntu, but confined.
264	│        ├─ Official Flathub → use flatpak (community.general.flatpak module).
265	│        │                    Cross-distro friendly, also confined.
266	│        └─ Community-only → skip; AppImage probably more reliable.
267	│
268	└─ Only AppImage / tarball?
269	   ├─ AppImage → drop in ~/Applications/ as <app>.AppImage. AIL integrates.
270	   └─ tarball  → ~/Applications/<app>/ + wrapper script + manual .desktop.
271	                 ⚠️ Last resort — no auto-update path, manual everything.
272	```
273	
274	### Concrete patterns
275	
276	**`.deb` pattern** — see "Install Cursor via .deb" in
277	[`gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](../../dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml).
278	Two-step:
279	
280	1. `ansible.builtin.uri` — fetch vendor's API to resolve the latest
281	   `.deb` URL (return JSON, parse `debUrl` or similar field).
282	2. `ansible.builtin.get_url` — download the `.deb`, with `force: true`
283	   (overwrite stale files from prior apply) and `until: cursor_dl is
284	   succeeded` + `retries: 4` + `delay: 5` (GFW-region CDN drops).
285	3. `ansible.builtin.apt: deb=<path>` — install. Postinst handles apt
286	   source if vendor ships one.
287	4. Wrap the whole block in `rescue:` that prints a manual-fallback URL.
288	
289	**AppImage pattern** — see "Install Zen Browser AppImage" in the same
290	file. Three-step:
291	
292	1. `ansible.builtin.uri` — GitHub releases API (or vendor equivalent)
293	   to resolve the asset URL.
294	2. `selectattr('name', 'match', '^<prefix>-<arch>\\.AppImage$')` filter
295	   to pick the right asset for `target_architecture` (already normalized
296	   to `x86_64` / `aarch64` by the `Set target_architecture from dpkg` task
297	   in [`linux.yml`](../../dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml)).
298	3. `ansible.builtin.get_url` to `~/Applications/<app>.AppImage` with
299	   `mode: '0755'` and a stable filename.
300	4. Write a `.desktop` entry under `~/.local/share/applications/` using
301	   `ansible.builtin.copy` with a `content:` literal — the file gets
302	   merged into the system menu via `update-desktop-database`.
303

309	    name: bitwarden
310	    state: present
311	    classic: false   # most apps are confined; set true only when vendor docs say so
312	  become: true
313	```

323	    method: user     # per-user install; `system` requires root

### 1. The `gui_apps_linux` role — mechanisms used

This role is **desktop-only** (runs only when the `gui_apps` tag is selected, which happens exclusively for `profile == ubuntu_desktop` — see section 3). It demonstrates every install mechanism the repo uses:

- **direct `.deb`** via `ansible.builtin.apt: deb=<path>` (Cursor, Discord)
- **Flatpak** (`community.general.flatpak` / `flatpak_remote`, per-user) and **Snap** (referenced in docs)
- **AppImage** dropped into `~/Applications/` (Zen Browser)
- **stock apt** (CopyQ, playerctl/wmctrl/xdotool)

Defaults are just two toggles: `gui_apps_linux_no_root` and `gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps`.

Important for Resilio: **Resilio Sync on Linux has no native GUI app** — the `resilio-sync` package is a headless daemon exposing a Web UI on `localhost:8888`. So the install is identical on desktop and server, and it does **not** belong in `gui_apps_linux` (which is skipped entirely on `ubuntu_server`).

### 2. The apt-repo-adding pattern (two variants in this repo)

**Variant A — modern `deb822_repository` (preferred, used by VSCode/Steam).** This is the closest match to what Resilio needs. From `gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` (VSCode, lines ~364-420):

```yaml
- name: Ensure /etc/apt/keyrings exists
  ansible.builtin.file: { path: /etc/apt/keyrings, state: directory, mode: '0755' }

- name: Add Microsoft GPG key (dearmored)
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -eu
    wget -qO- https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc \
      | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
  args: { creates: /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg }

- name: Remove legacy one-line VSCode source (pre-deb822 format)
  ansible.builtin.file: { path: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/vscode.list, state: absent }

- name: Add VSCode apt repository (deb822)
  ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
    name: vscode
    types: deb
    uris: https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/code
    suites: stable
    components: main
    architectures: "{{ {'x86_64': 'amd64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture] }}"
    signed_by: /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg

- name: Refresh apt cache (VSCode repo)
  ansible.builtin.apt: { update_cache: true }

- name: Install VSCode package
  ansible.builtin.apt: { name: code, state: present }
```
Wrapped in a `block:`/`rescue:` where the rescue does `deb822_repository: { name: vscode, state: absent }` so a failed install never leaves a broken source that breaks later `apt update` runs. Note: `deb822_repository` requires `python3-debian` (installed by the `base` role) and does **not** run `apt update` itself.

For Resilio (`deb http://linux-packages.resilio.com/resilio-sync/deb resilio-sync non-free`) the deb822 form maps to: `uris: http://linux-packages.resilio.com/resilio-sync/deb`, `suites: resilio-sync`, `components: non-free`, `signed_by: /etc/apt/keyrings/resilio-sync.gpg`.

**Variant B — legacy one-line source (used by ngrok).** In `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml` (~lines 736-764): `get_url` the `.asc`, `gpg --dearmor` into `/etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg`, then `ansible.builtin.copy` a `content: "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg] <uri> ..."` to `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/ngrok.list`, then `apt: {name, update_cache: true}`. It also has a user-level tarball fallback. Prefer Variant A for new code — the repo is actively migrating off one-line sources (each deb822 block explicitly deletes the legacy `.list` first). Every role additionally self-gates on `ansible_facts['os_family']` and `target_architecture` (normalized to `x86_64`/`aarch64`/`armv7l` in the playbook `pre_tasks`).
- `noRoot` mode adds `--skip-tags sudo`; system apt/deb tasks are all tagged `tags: [sudo]`.

So the pattern to make a tool available on **both** desktop and server is: give the role its own tag + a chezmoi `installResilioSync` boolean, and append the tag for `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` (both profiles), mirroring `homelab_tools`/`auditd`.

Two existing patterns:

- **System-level unit file install** — `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/niri/tasks/main.yml` (~lines 168-184) copies unit files to `/etc/systemd/user/*.service` via `ansible.builtin.copy` with `remote_src`. Role has `resources/*.service` files it ships.
- **Rootless daemon with `systemctl --user` lifecycle** — `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/docker/tasks/main.yml` is the best template for a background daemon. It shows the full pattern:
  - `ansible.builtin.systemd_service` with `scope: user`, `enabled: true`, `state: started`, and `environment: { XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: "/run/user/{{ ansible_facts['user_uid'] }}" }`
  - `loginctl enable-linger {{ user }}` (with `creates: /var/lib/systemd/linger/<user>`) so the user service survives logout — **critical for a headless server sync daemon**
  - disabling the rootful system unit via `ansible.builtin.systemd_service: { enabled: false, state: stopped }`

Note: `homelab_tools` (`/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/homelab_tools/tasks/main.yml`) deliberately does **not** enable services — line ~247 comment: *"smartd / ipmievd services are intentionally NOT enabled. This repo is install-only."* So enabling a systemd service is a conscious opt-in decision you'd be making for Resilio.

Resilio's `.deb` postinst ships both a system unit (`/lib/systemd/system/resilio-sync.service`) and a user template (`resilio-sync@.service`). ## 1. Brewfile structure and where a cask goes

Three Brewfiles, all chezmoi templates, live in `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/homebrew/`:

- `Brewfile.tmpl` — shared/cross-platform (taps + a few formulae like `mas`, `tailscale`). Deployed to `~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile`.
- `Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` — **macOS GUI apps (casks) + Mac App Store apps**. Deployed to `~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin`. **This is where `resilio-sync` goes.**
- `Brewfile.linux.tmpl` — Linux.

Casks (GUI) live exclusively in `Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`; formulae (CLI) go in `Brewfile.tmpl` (shared) or the platform files. The comment at the top of `Brewfile.tmpl` (lines 16-17) explicitly notes most CLI tools are managed by ansible, not the Brewfile — so a GUI cask like Resilio Sync belongs in the Brewfile, not ansible.

## 2. Cask declaration pattern (grouping + comments)

Casks are grouped under banner-comment section headers, one `cask "name"` per line, with inline `#` comments for descriptions and commented-out lines for optional/disabled apps. Representative snippet from `Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` (lines 47-60):

```
{{ if .installBrewApps -}}
# =============================================================================
# Casks - System Utilities
# =============================================================================
cask "nikitabobko/tap/aerospace"  # Tiling window manager
cask "alt-tab"                     # Windows-style alt-tab
cask "raycast"                     # Spotlight replacement
cask "maccy"                       # Plaintext-SQLite clipboard history ...
# cask "itsycal"                     # Menu bar calendar   (disabled example)
cask "the-unarchiver"              # Archive extraction
```

Sections present: Terminals & Editors, AI & Coding Assistants, System Utilities, Communication, Browsers, Productivity, Media & Entertainment, Gaming, Finance & Trading, Network & VPN, Virtualization & Remote, Developer Tools, Cloud Storage (Chinese apps), then Mac App Store (`mas`) entries.

**Best fit for `resilio-sync`:** it's a file-sync tool, so the natural home is the **Cloud Storage** section (`Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` lines 144-149), which currently only holds a commented-out `baidunetdisk`. It sits alongside `cask "google-drive"` (Productivity section, line 84) conceptually. Suggested line:

```
cask "resilio-sync"   # P2P file sync (BitTorrent Sync) — background daemon + menu bar
```

Note the whole general-cask block is gated by `{{ if .installBrewApps -}}` (opens line 47, and the Cloud Storage section is inside the block that closes at line 161). So the new cask must go **before** the `{{ end -}}` on line 161 to be governed by `installBrewApps`. The Cloud Storage section additionally shows a nested per-cask gate pattern using `{{ if .useChineseMirror -}}` (lines 147-149) if you ever want conditional install.

## 3. How brew bundle runs + macOS/flag gating

`brew bundle` is **not** run by an ansible role anymore. The `homebrew` role (`/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/homebrew/tasks/main.yml`) only installs/updates/cleans Homebrew itself. The `macos.yml` playbook (`/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/playbooks/macos.yml`, lines 93-94) explicitly delegates bundling to a chezmoi script:

`/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl`

That script re-runs on Brewfile hash change (hashes at lines 19-26), sets `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, runs the shared Brewfile then `Brewfile.darwin` with retry logic.

Gating happens on three levels:
- **chezmoi OS gate:** `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}` throughout the script and Brewfiles (e.g. `Brewfile.tmpl` lines 10, 21).
- **Feature flags** (defined in `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`): `installBrewApps` (line 86, general GUI apps — **this governs the section where resilio-sync goes**), `installAiDesktopApps` (line 34), `installGamingApps` (line 94). Defaults all `false`, set via `promptBoolOnce`.
- **Arch gate:** `{{ if eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64" -}}` for a few casks (chatgpt, codex-app, superset).

Ansible `when:` conditions are used elsewhere but not for casks; the cask path is entirely chezmoi-template-gated.

## 4. Closest daemon / login-item analog

There is **no repo-managed launchd plist, login-item, or `brew services` entry for any cask** — the repo installs casks purely via `brew bundle` and lets each app manage its own background/login-item lifecycle through macOS. (The only `launchctl`/`LaunchAgents` references are read-only observability tooling: `dot_config/shell/29_log_tools.sh` `svcstat`, `dot_config/shell/45_audit.sh.tmpl`, and Television channels `services.toml.tmpl` / `scheduled-jobs.toml.tmpl`.)

The closest functional analogs to a sync daemon, all installed as plain casks with no extra handling, are:

- `cask "maccy"` (line 54), `cask "ollama-app"` (line 42) — other background/menu-bar apps.

**Bottom line:** adding `cask "resilio-sync"` to the Cloud Storage section of `Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` (before line 161's `{{ end -}}`, inside the `installBrewApps` block) is all that's required — it will be installed automatically by the `run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl` script on the next `chezmoi apply` for any darwin host with `installBrewApps = true`. No ansible role, launchd plist, or login-item wiring exists or is needed; follow the `google-drive` precedent.

## Report: How this repo installs Linux apps, and where Resilio Sync fits

### 1. The `gui_apps_linux` role — mechanisms used

- Tasks: `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`
- Defaults: `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/defaults/main.yml`

This role is **desktop-only** (runs only when the `gui_apps` tag is selected, which happens exclusively for `profile == ubuntu_desktop` — see section 3). It demonstrates every install mechanism the repo uses:
- **cargo build** (Alacritty), with a hand-written `.desktop` entry + icon + `update-desktop-database`
- **Third-party apt repo** via `ansible.builtin.deb822_repository` (VSCode → Microsoft repo; Steam → Valve repo)
- **PPA** via `deb822_repository` (AppImageLauncher, with GitHub `.deb` fallback)
- **direct `.deb`** via `ansible.builtin.apt: deb=<path>` (Cursor, Discord)
- **Flatpak** (`community.general.flatpak` / `flatpak_remote`, per-user) and **Snap** (referenced in docs)
- **AppImage** dropped into `~/Applications/` (Zen Browser)
- **stock apt** (CopyQ, playerctl/wmctrl/xdotool)

Defaults are just two toggles: `gui_apps_linux_no_root` and `gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps`.

Important for Resilio: **Resilio Sync on Linux has no native GUI app** — the `resilio-sync` package is a headless daemon exposing a Web UI on `localhost:8888`. So the install is identical on desktop and server, and it does **not** belong in `gui_apps_linux` (which is skipped entirely on `ubuntu_server`).

### 2. The apt-repo-adding pattern (two variants in this repo)

**Variant A — modern `deb822_repository` (preferred, used by VSCode/Steam).** This is the closest match to what Resilio needs. From `gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml` (VSCode, lines ~364-420):

```yaml
- name: Ensure /etc/apt/keyrings exists
  ansible.builtin.file: { path: /etc/apt/keyrings, state: directory, mode: '0755' }

- name: Add Microsoft GPG key (dearmored)
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -eu
    wget -qO- https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc \
      | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
  args: { creates: /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg }

- name: Remove legacy one-line VSCode source (pre-deb822 format)
  ansible.builtin.file: { path: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/vscode.list, state: absent }

- name: Add VSCode apt repository (deb822)
  ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
    name: vscode
    types: deb
    uris: https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/code
    suites: stable
    components: main
    architectures: "{{ {'x86_64': 'amd64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture] }}"
    signed_by: /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg

- name: Refresh apt cache (VSCode repo)
  ansible.builtin.apt: { update_cache: true }

- name: Install VSCode package
  ansible.builtin.apt: { name: code, state: present }
```
Wrapped in a `block:`/`rescue:` where the rescue does `deb822_repository: { name: vscode, state: absent }` so a failed install never leaves a broken source that breaks later `apt update` runs. Note: `deb822_repository` requires `python3-debian` (installed by the `base` role) and does **not** run `apt update` itself.

For Resilio (`deb http://linux-packages.resilio.com/resilio-sync/deb resilio-sync non-free`) the deb822 form maps to: `uris: http://linux-packages.resilio.com/resilio-sync/deb`, `suites: resilio-sync`, `components: non-free`, `signed_by: /etc/apt/keyrings/resilio-sync.gpg`.

**Variant B — legacy one-line source (used by ngrok).** In `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/networking_tools/tasks/main.yml` (~lines 736-764): `get_url` the `.asc`, `gpg --dearmor` into `/etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg`, then `ansible.builtin.copy` a `content: "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/ngrok.gpg] <uri> ..."` to `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/ngrok.list`, then `apt: {name, update_cache: true}`. It also has a user-level tarball fallback. Prefer Variant A for new code — the repo is actively migrating off one-line sources (each deb822 block explicitly deletes the legacy `.list` first). The Steam block (lines ~657-745) additionally shows scoped `apt-get update -o Dir::Etc::sourcelist=sources.list.d/steam.sources` to refresh only one source.

### 3. Profile gating (ubuntu_desktop vs ubuntu_server)

Gating is **not** done inside ansible with a `profile` var. It's done at the **tag-selection layer** in the run_onchange wrapper: `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`.

- The `profile` prompt is defined in `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` (line ~20): choices `macos | ubuntu_desktop | ubuntu_server | centos_server`, default `ubuntu_server`.
- The wrapper builds a `TAGS` string per profile (lines ~199-218):
  - `ubuntu_desktop`: `...,gui_apps` (GUI role included)
  - `ubuntu_server`: same base set **minus** `nerdfonts`/`gui_apps` (no GUI)
- Optional roles are appended by chezmoi `installX` booleans, e.g. `installHomelabTools` → `,homelab_tools` (gated `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"`), `installNiri` → `,niri` (gated `eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop"`), `installNetworkingTools` → `,networking_tools`, etc. (lines ~234-291).
- The playbook `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml` lists **all** roles unconditionally; the `--tags` selection is what actually gates them. Every role additionally self-gates on `ansible_facts['os_family']` and `target_architecture` (normalized to `x86_64`/`aarch64`/`armv7l` in the playbook `pre_tasks`).
- `noRoot` mode adds `--skip-tags sudo`; system apt/deb tasks are all tagged `tags: [sudo]`.

So the pattern to make a tool available on **both** desktop and server is: give the role its own tag + a chezmoi `installResilioSync` boolean, and append the tag for `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` (both profiles), mirroring `homelab_tools`/`auditd`.

### 4. Systemd / daemon patterns (the key part for Resilio)

Two existing patterns:

- **System-level unit file install** — `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/niri/tasks/main.yml` (~lines 168-184) copies unit files to `/etc/systemd/user/*.service` via `ansible.builtin.copy` with `remote_src`. Role has `resources/*.service` files it ships.
- **Rootless daemon with `systemctl --user` lifecycle** — `/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/docker/tasks/main.yml` is the best template for a background daemon. It shows the full pattern:
  - `ansible.builtin.systemd_service` with `scope: user`, `enabled: true`, `state: started`, and `environment: { XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: "/run/user/{{ ansible_facts['user_uid'] }}" }`
  - `loginctl enable-linger {{ user }}` (with `creates: /var/lib/systemd/linger/<user>`) so the user service survives logout — **critical for a headless server sync daemon**
  - disabling the rootful system unit via `ansible.builtin.systemd_service: { enabled: false, state: stopped }`

Note: `homelab_tools` (`/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/homelab_tools/tasks/main.yml`) deliberately does **not** enable services — line ~247 comment: *"smartd / ipmievd services are intentionally NOT enabled. This repo is install-only."* So enabling a systemd service is a conscious opt-in decision you'd be making for Resilio.

Resilio's `.deb` postinst ships both a system unit (`/lib/systemd/system/resilio-sync.service`) and a user template (`resilio-sync@.service`). You can either enable the system service (`ansible.builtin.systemd_service: {name: resilio-sync, enabled: true, state: started}` under `tags: [sudo]`) or the user-scoped one following the Docker `scope: user` + `enable-linger` pattern.

### 5. Where a new Resilio Sync tool best fits

Because Resilio is a headless daemon needed on **both** `ubuntu_server` and `ubuntu_desktop`, it should **not** go in `gui_apps_linux` (desktop-only, skipped on server). Best fit is a **new dedicated role** `dot_ansible/roles/resilio_sync/` following the `homelab_tools`/`docker` conventions:
- `tasks/main.yml`: self-gate on `ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'` (+ RedHat branch if wanted); add the apt repo via **deb822_repository Variant A** (key to `/etc/apt/keyrings/resilio-sync.gpg`, all under `tags: [sudo]`, wrapped in `block:`/`rescue:` that removes the source on failure); `apt: {name: resilio-sync}`; then optionally enable the systemd service (system unit under `tags: [sudo]`, or user unit via the Docker `scope: user` + `enable-linger` pattern).
- `defaults/main.yml`: toggles like `resilio_sync_enable_service`, mirroring `homelab_tools` defaults.
- Register the role in `dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml` with `tags: [resilio_sync]`.
- Add a `resilio_sync` role-hash line to the run_onchange wrapper's header (lines ~7-47) so edits re-trigger, plus a tag-append block: add an `installResilioSync` prompt in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` and, in the wrapper, `{{ if and $installResilioSync (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") }}TAGS="${TAGS},resilio_sync"{{ end }}` (following the `homelab_tools` block at lines ~284-287) so it lands on both Linux profiles.

**On Linux, how should the Resilio Sync daemon run? (It's used for your files/photos, so file access matters.)**

Options:
- **Per-user service (recommended)** - Runs as YOUR user via `systemctl --user` + enable-linger (survives logout). Config in ~/.config/resilio-sync, direct access to your home files — best for photo backup to NAS. Follows the repo's Docker-rootless precedent.
- **System service (.deb default)** - Runs as the dedicated `rslsync` system user via the package's default systemd unit. More isolated, but you must grant `rslsync` permission to any folders you sync.
- **Install only, don't enable** - Just install the package (matches repo's strict install-only convention like homelab_tools). You enable/start the service yourself later.

**How should installation be gated across your machines?**

Options:
- **New installResilioSync prompt (recommended)** - One dedicated chezmoi prompt flag gates BOTH the Linux ansible role AND the macOS cask. Off by default; opt in per machine. Consistent with installHomelabTools/installNiri pattern.
- **Fold into existing flags** - macOS cask under the existing installBrewApps flag; Linux always installs on any Linux host. No new prompt, but less control per-machine.


**Answer:** Per-user service (recommended), New installResilioSync prompt (recommended)
